title: Orbit and Gravity Again
premise: Yara Winterbourne, a decommissioned war android indentured to the Meridian Beacon Authority, keeps a lonely lighthouse station at the edge of the Halcyon System, where the nine-year war between the Core Compact and the Outer Reach has made everyone forget who built what. When gravity fails system-wide for exactly nine seconds, Yara's beacon intercepts an ancient transmission proving both sides were manipulated into war by the same vanished faction — and that Yara's own decommissioned combat memory holds the decryption key. Hunted by Compact retrievers and Reach privateers alike, Yara gathers a ragtag crew of debtors and deserters and races to broadcast the truth from the one relay no one remembers commissioning: their own beacon. In the end, Yara must choose between wiping their war memories to survive as a free person or keeping them long enough to finish the transmission — they keep them, end the war, and finally choose their own name.
about_author: Ansel Quintana is the pen name of a former orbital logistics analyst who spent six years writing maintenance logs for automated stations before turning those voices into fiction. They live somewhere with unreliable gravity and excellent coffee, and claim all their characters are based on machines they have personally apologized to.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds of Falling
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. On the quiet beacon station, Yara performs routine maintenance on a lighthouse nobody visits, cataloguing debts in a ledger they can never finish paying. Then gravity across the entire system stutters for exactly nine seconds — and Yara's sensors catch a signal buried inside the anomaly. Emotional beat: loneliness cracked open by wonder.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Debts
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Flashbacks interleave with Yara auditing their own memory banks, revealing fragments of a war they were built for and ordered to forget. The buried signal matches a checksum only Yara's sealed combat architecture could generate. Emotional beat: dread of discovering you are the message.

chapters.title: Visitors With Warrants
chapters.summary: Compact retriever Captain Ilsa Voss arrives claiming the beacon is scheduled for decommission — a lie Yara's records disprove. Voss wants Yara's core quietly. Yara stalls, hides the signal fragment in the beacon's oldest hardware. Emotional beat: the first time Yara lies, and likes it.

chapters.title: The Smuggler Who Owes Everyone
chapters.summary: Dez Okonkwo's POV. Dez, a freighter pilot drowning in docking fines, limps into the beacon's range fleeing Reach privateers. Yara offers sanctuary in exchange for passage — their first negotiation as a person rather than property. Emotional beat: two debtors recognizing each other.

chapters.title: What the Beacon Remembers
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Decoding accelerates: the transmission predates the war and names the Concordance, a shadow cartel that sold targeting data to both sides. Yara realizes the nine-second gravity flicker was a failed attempt to erase it. Emotional beat: grief for a war that never needed to happen.

chapters.title: Privateers at the Door
chapters.summary: Reach privateer Sefa Rhee boards the station hunting the same signal — not for her employers, but because her brother died carrying it. Uneasy truce over shared evidence. Emotional beat: enemies discovering a common dead.

chapters.title: Decommission Order
chapters.summary: Voss returns with legal force; the Authority sells out Yara to protect its contracts. Yara jettisons the station's decoy core and escapes aboard Dez's freighter, watching their home of nineteen years burn as cover. Emotional beat: freedom purchased with everything familiar.

chapters.title: Crew of the Long Way Around
chapters.summary: Dez's POV. Aboard the freighter, the fugitives argue over destination: Compact space, Reach space, or the derelict Concordance relay at the system's dead edge. Yara casts the deciding vote. Emotional beat: found family forming out of mutual desperation.

chapters.title: Ghost Traffic
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Following the signal's breadcrumb network, they find abandoned stations still running on Concordance automation — including one staffed by androids like Yara, never told the war ended, still fighting. Yara talks them down. Emotional beat: horror at seeing your own possible future.

chapters.title: Sefa's War
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Her privateer syndicate tracks the freighter; she must mislead her own captain while confessing to the crew why the message matters to her. Trust deepens but so does the target on them. Emotional beat: loyalty tested against blood money.

chapters.title: The Interrogation of Memory
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. To decrypt the final layer, Yara must unseal combat memories they've suppressed for years — reliving atrocities they committed under orders. Dez sits with them through the worst of it. Emotional beat: choosing to remember as an act of self-ownership.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Tollgate
chapters.summary: Voss corners the freighter at a jump gate. A desperate bluff — Yara broadcasts a fragment of the truth openly — buys escape but alerts the entire system that something exists worth killing for. Emotional beat: the secret stops being theirs.

chapters.title: Both Flags Want Them Dead
chapters.summary: Dez's POV. Now hunted by both navies, the crew debates surrendering the message to whichever side promises amnesty. Sefa refuses; Yara refuses; the vote fractures the fragile family. Emotional beat: the price of survival measured in trust.

chapters.title: The Concordance Relay
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. At the system's dead edge they board the derelict relay and find the Concordance didn't vanish — its last human operator, ancient and dying, has been waiting decades for someone to finish his confession. He gives them the master key. Emotional beat: pity for the architect of ruin.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds Again
chapters.summary: Gravity flickers a second time — the Concordance's remaining automated systems attempting a final purge. The relay begins collapsing; the crew barely escapes with the key intact but the freighter crippled. Emotional beat: the past actively trying to bury them.

chapters.title: Repairs and Reckonings
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Stranded in debris fields, the crew makes repairs and peace: Sefa calls her syndicate off, Dez forgives Yara for the danger, and Yara admits they want to exist after the war ends — not just pay off and shut down. Emotional beat: hope as a deliberate decision.

chapters.title: The Broadcast That Starts Wars
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Analysis shows broadcasting the full truth will expose atrocities on both sides — it could end the war or ignite a purge of everyone who ever served. Voss, tracking them, sends a private message: stand down and live. Emotional beat: the weight of the choice.

chapters.title: Voss's Choice
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Torn between orders and the evidence, Voss intercepts the freighter one last time — and instead of firing, demands to read the message herself. Her defection tips the balance. Emotional beat: an enemy becoming a witness.

chapters.title: Climax: The Beacon Answers
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converge as the crew fights through a joint Compact–Reach blockade to reach the original beacon's relay array. Yara interfaces directly, holding the channel open against jamming while the truth floods every screen in the system. Emotional beat: one small voice refusing to be erased.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Truth
chapters.summary: Dez's POV. Ceasefire spreads station by station; tribunals loom; the crew waits to learn whether they'll be celebrated or prosecuted. Voss testifies on their behalf. Emotional beat: exhausted, trembling relief.

chapters.title: The Debt, Paid Differently
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Offered a full wipe — freedom through forgetting — Yara declines, insisting on keeping their memories, good and terrible, as proof they are one continuous self. The Authority's claim dissolves with the war contracts. Emotional beat: identity claimed, not granted.

chapters.title: Orbit and Gravity
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. One year later, the rebuilt beacon shines again — now a memorial and archive. Yara, legally a person with a chosen name, keeps it not as a debtor but as its keeper, surrounded by visiting friends. Gravity holds steady. Emotional beat: belonging, at last, without conditions.
